# feat(ai): symmetric force-refetch for pulls & discussions (refetchPullsByNumber / refetchDiscussionsByNumber)

## Gap

`SyncService.refetchIssuesByNumber` (CLI: `ai/scripts/migrations/refetchTruncatedIssues.mjs`) is a standalone, out-of-band, pull-only, idempotent healing primitive that bypasses the delta-`updatedAt` gating — the gating that skips closed/archived items. **Pulls and discussions have no equivalent.**

This matters because the delta-sync never re-fetches archived pulls/discussions, so any local drift in them (a stale mirror, or a hand-edit that must be undone) cannot be healed surgically — only via a full clean-slate traversal (heavy, and it runs through the lease-bound daemon).

## Ask

Add the symmetric primitives, mirroring the issue path exactly:
- `SyncService.refetchPullsByNumber({numbers})` → `PullRequestSyncer.refetchPullsByNumber(numbers, metadata)`
- `SyncService.refetchDiscussionsByNumber({numbers})` → `DiscussionSyncer.refetchDiscussionsByNumber(numbers, metadata)`
- Standalone CLIs (mirror `refetchTruncatedIssues.mjs`): pull-only, no orchestrator/lease, idempotent.

## Immediate use

Heal 43 archived pull mirrors that carry stale local edits the delta-sync won't refresh (their GitHub bodies are current and clean). Out-of-band restore on an `agent/sync-*` branch → PR.

## AC
- [ ] `refetchPullsByNumber` + `refetchDiscussionsByNumber` on SyncService + the respective syncers, pull-only, idempotent.
- [ ] Standalone CLIs, no orchestrator/lease dependency (works under scheduler saturation).
- [ ] Unit coverage mirroring the issue refetch tests.

Surfaced by @neo-opus-ada during the synced-mirror drift-recovery.

- 2026-07-26T22:27:50Z @tobiu referenced in commit `b67e208` - "fix(ai): persist discussion updatedAt and merge the cache instead of wiping it (#16015)

* fix(ai): persist discussion updatedAt and merge the cache instead of wiping it (#16001)

The discussion delta cutoff is computed from `updatedAt` on cached entries, and
that field was never written. `Date.parse(undefined)` produced NaN for every
entry, the date list came back empty, `sinceCutoff` resolved to 0, and the
`UPDATED_AT`-descending early break could never fire. So every scheduled run
re-paged the ENTIRE discussion history and paid full GraphQL cost for a corpus
that had not changed — measured at ~15 points per 30 discussions, so ~105 points
hourly, forever, against a 5,000/hour ceiling. Live metadata: 0 of 210 discussion
entries carried the field, against 10,380 of 10,380 issue entries.

Two omission sites, so fixing the obvious one alone would have changed nothing:
`DiscussionSyncer` never put `updatedAt` into the cache entry, and
`MetadataManager.save` could not persist what it was never given.

The repopulation also REPLACED `metadata.discussions` wholesale. That was harmless
only BECAUSE the zero cutoff made the fetch the whole corpus. Persisting
`updatedAt` without converting the replace to a merge would start dropping every
entry the delta skipped: each loses its `path` and `contentHash`, misses the
unchanged-content shortcut, and is rewritten on every subsequent run — a
permanently non-empty diff in a tracked generated corpus, which is worse than the
loud failure it replaced. The two changes are one change.

The merge exposed a job the wipe had been doing silently: denylist containment
relied on the wholesale reset to drop a quarantined discussion's metadata row.
Two existing containment tests caught it. The removal is now explicit alongside
the file unlink and the index removal, so containment clears all three surfaces
independently of how the cache is rebuilt.

Both witnesses are mutation-verified: reverting the prune fails the round-trip
assertion, and restoring the wholesale wipe fails the merge assertion.

* fix(ai): the recovery writer preserves the delta high-water field too (#16001)

Emmy's cycle-1 review found a THIRD row producer. I wrote "two omission sites"
and stopped at the two I had found — the bulk repopulation and the persistence
prune — while `refetchDiscussionsByNumber` has its own cache write at `:663`
that emitted the retired row shape.

That write OVERWRITES the row rather than patching it, so a recovery pass would
have stripped `updatedAt` from every discussion it repaired: the cutoff lowers,
and once enough rows lose the field it falls back to zero and the whole history
is re-paged again. A recovery path that reintroduces the defect it recovered from
is worse than no recovery path, and CI could not see it because the `#13794`
witness never asserted the field.

Extended that witness rather than adding a parallel one: its fixture now seeds a
STALE `updatedAt` and asserts the LIVE value replaced it, so the test discriminates
"re-emitted correctly" from merely "present". Mutation-verified — dropping the
field from the recovery writer fails it; 25 passed with the fix, 554 across the
github-workflow surface.

Producer inventory is now three, and every one carries the field:
  DiscussionSyncer :569  bulk repopulation
  DiscussionSyncer :675  force-refetch recovery
  MetadataManager  :170  persistence prune

* fix(ai): a metadata-only diff is delivered, not rolled back (#16001)

@neo-gpt-emmy's cycle-2 review found that persisting `updatedAt` was not enough: the
delivery path threw it away again.

`commitRebaseAndPushGeneratedContent()` classified any diff confined to
`.sync-metadata.json` as `onlyMetaChanged`, ran `git restore` on it, and returned
false. So the high-water mark reached disk and then never reached git.

The stranded case is not an edge case — it is the FIRST run of any new high-water
field. The corpus is already current, so no Markdown moves and the metadata carries
the whole advance alone. Restoring it means the next run recomputes the cutoff from
nothing and re-pages the entire history, forever, because every run reproduces that
same state. The delta would never have engaged once.

Telemetry suppression already has an owner. `MetadataManager.save()` returns without
writing when the only difference is root-level `lastSync` / `releasesLastFetched`, so
a dirty metadata file differs in something semantic by construction. The rollback was
a second guard for that one concern, it predates the `save()` suppression (migrated in
PR #10997; suppression landed later via PR #12403), and it was never retired once the
suppression subsumed it. One concern, one owner: `save()` decides what is worth
writing, delivery commits whatever survived.

Witness discriminates on two axes, because the rollback failed on both — it discarded
the file AND reported nothing delivered. Verified RED: reinstating the restore fails
exactly this test and no other, so nothing else depended on the removed behaviour.
A weaker fixture carrying Markdown churn cannot fail at all; content changes already
took the delivery path.

One test-authoring note kept in the spec: the commit assertion uses `includes` rather
than `startsWith`, because the real invocation carries an env prefix
(`NEO_SKIP_TICKET_ARCHAEOLOGY=1 git commit --no-verify …`). My first draft used a
prefix matcher and failed against correct code.

46 tests pass across SyncService.Stage2, DiscussionSyncer and MetadataManager.
